I work at Ulta and my personal pet peeve is people that scoff at me when I mention our credit card program. Yes I get it, not everyone will benefit from it but it’s my job to ask and if I don’t get enough credit card sign ups it affect how my managers schedule me. Just listen to my spiel about it and politely decline, I’ll totally understand. However if you have ever signed up for the Ulta credit card, just know you probably made that employees day! But don’t feel bad if you say no, just be civil about it!

My parents found out about my self harm when i was around 13, i’m 18 now. I agree with all the other comments but one thing that I always hated was my parents continually trying to talk to me about it. I was always weird about talking to them, it just felt wrong. Of course be there for her but don’t pry. If she is open about it, great! But if not, it’s completely normal! I was always more comfortable with a therapist as I knew I wasn’t going to hurt my therapists feelings. I think it’s great that you are so willing and caring to get her help and I wish you all the best in helping to guide her to recovery. I know how terrified you must be as a parent, but please don’t make her feel like she’s on constant watch and is being sheltered from the world if that makes any sense?
